_comment: OIDF conformance test-plan configuration — FAPI 2.0 Security Profile (Final),
OpenID Provider, PKI mutual-TLS client authentication variant (X5.2).
Placeholders of the form ${NAME} are substituted by
conformance/scripts/render-plan.sh from conformance/suite.env, so this file
is committed with no client ids, no secrets and no host-specific paths. The
rendered copy lands under conformance/.run/ (gitignored) and is what the
suite actually reads.
Plan name to select in the suite UI or the API:
fapi2-security-profile-final-test-plan
with variant { client_auth_type: mtls, sender_constrain: mtls,
fapi_client_type: plain_oauth, openid: plain_oauth,
fapi_request_method: pushed }.
Why 'pushed' rather than 'unsigned': FAPI 2.0 §5.3.1.2 requires PAR, and a
fapi2-profile AXIAM client is registered require_par=true, so a plan run
with an unpushed request method would fail every authorization step for a
reason that is the profile working correctly. See the runbook.
W9 correction, found by the first run that ever submitted this plan to the
suite. The variant block carried `fapi_client_type`, which the suite
rejects outright:
Unknown variant parameter(s) [fapi_client_type] for plan
'fapi2-security-profile-final-test-plan'
so NO plan could be created from any of these three templates, and no FAPI
module has ever run from them. `fapi_client_type` is a FAPI 1.0 variant;
FAPI 2.0 expresses the same choice as `openid`, which these templates were
already setting to the same value, so removing it loses nothing.
`fapi_profile` is stated explicitly rather than left to default, because a
certification result should say which profile it certifies.
And a second correction from the same run: `fapi_request_method` and
`fapi_response_mode` were removed as well. They are MODULE-level variants
that the plan fixes for each of its own modules, so supplying them here is
not merely redundant — the suite refuses the whole plan:
Variant 'fapi_request_method' has been set by user, but test plan
already sets this variant for module
'fapi2-security-profile-final-discovery-end-point-verification'
The paragraph above about `pushed` still describes what happens; it is the
plan that arranges it, not this file.
W9, third correction from the first run. The discovery URL carried
`?tenant_id=${AXIAM_TENANT_ID}` and the suite failed the very first module:
CheckOauthDiscEndpointIssuer: issuer listed in the discovery document is
not consistent with the location the discovery document was retrieved
from. These must match to prevent impersonation attacks.
OIDC Discovery §4.1 ties the retrieval location to the `issuer` claim, and
a query parameter breaks that correspondence. W7 made the document
tenant-aware through exactly such a parameter, so a tenant-scoped discovery
URL cannot be a conformance plan's discoveryUrl. The FAPI lane loses
nothing by dropping it — it requests only `openid`, and the parameter's
sole effect is to advertise the `address` and `phone` scopes. What it costs
the BASIC lane is recorded in docs/conformance/ and in the plan's §4.10.
